Fairer housing support - the Review of Social Housing includes changes to Income Related Rent, the Accommodation Supplement, and Temporary Additional Support from 1 April 2027. There will also be changes to transitional and emergency housing subsidies in line with changes to Income Related Rent. 

Incentivising housing growth and supporting the implementation of the Going for Housing Growth programme, through the Incentives for Growth Fund.

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">In real estate speak, it’s a “buyers’ market” right now – but does that mean it is a first home buyers’ market? 

What the mortgage lending data from the Reserve Bank shows us is that there’s been a steady recent increase in first home buyer activity.

Since 2021, when first home buyers made up just 25% of new mortgages, the first home buyers’ segment increased to 34% for most of 2025.

So why are first home buyers so active? There are two reasons for this. Firstly, deposit affordability has improved as house prices remain static whilst wages grow. Also, nearly half of first home buyers are buying without the traditional 20% deposit. 

Secondly, mortgage payments are more affordable because interest rates have fallen. And this is happening against a backdrop of continuing high volumes of homes for sale.

It really is a (first home) buyers’ market, for now.
